one_line: QAOA Max-Cut demo ran as described; shows modest robustness at ~1e-3 2Q error but doesn’t test quantum advantage.
key_finding: For n=10 Max-Cut, QAOA p=1–2 retains nearly the same approximation ratio under depolarizing noise with p2=1e-3, with only ~0.4–0.6% absolute degradation.
reasoning: The reported circuit depths/CX counts, optimized parameters, and noiseless vs noisy expectation values are internally consistent and include a quantitative noise sweep, indicating the experiment likely ran as claimed. The results support the essay’s near-term emphasis on shallow variational algorithms being usable under ~1e-3 two-qubit error rates, at least for this small instance and depolarizing model. However, the study is too small (n=10) to speak to the paper’s other core theme—tasks beyond classical simulation with 50–100 qubits—and it does not benchmark against classical heuristics beyond the exact optimum. The noise model is simplified (no SPAM, coherence, connectivity/compilation effects), so the characterization of the “realistic” NISQ regime is suggestive rather than definitive.
